passage: In craft period at school, Omkar folded a sheet of paper in half and pressed the crease flat with the side of his hand. On the front he drew a cake with three candles. Inside he wrote in careful letters, "To Chinmay." Last of all he took the pink and yellow crayons and coloured the cake and the flames. The teacher walked past. "Lovely." Omkar held the card up at arm's length and looked at it.

qa.q: What did Omkar draw on the front of the card?
qa.a: Omkar drew a cake with three candles.

qa.q: What was Omkar feeling as he held the card up at arm's length?
qa.a: Omkar felt proud and pleased with his card. He looked at it carefully after finishing.

qa.q: What could Omkar do if he was not sure what to write inside, and why?
qa.a: He could ask the teacher for ideas or look at another child's card. A word or two can help a card feel finished.

qa.q: How would the card look to Chinmay?
qa.a: Chinmay would get a card with a name inside and a cake with candles. It shows that someone remembered.

grounding: A child folds the paper, draws a cake, writes Chinmay's name inside and colours last so the card comes together.
